newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-ICI sells bulk chemicals to DuPont.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-ICI sells bulk chemicals to DuPont.

text.p: British chemicals giant ICI on Monday pulled off its second coup in as many months with the sale of half its bulk chemical operations to DuPont Co of the U.S. for $3 billion.
The rapid sale of its polyester and most of its titanium dioxide operations will go a long way to foot the $8 billion bill for Unilever Plc's speciality chemicals business which ICI picked up in May.

ICI chief executive Charles Miller Smith, credited with bringing a new vim and vigour to the grand old warhorse of Britain's chemicals industry, said the sale was a "decisive step" in his goal of moving ICI from the unpredictable world of bulk chemicals and into the high margin, consumer-led niches of speciality chemicals.
"This is another major milestone in creating a new ICI for the new century," a buoyant Miller Smith said.
ICI was immediately rewarded for its efforts by the stock market, which marked ICI's shares up 71 pence to 881 1/2 pence, the highest levels seen since May 1996.

Some analysts predicted the stock could reach the ten pound level over the next few weeks as it is re-rated to reflect the higher quality of earnings expected from its new product range, which includes items like industrial adhesives, starches and food ingredients.

Monday's disposal, which follows a 100 million pound sale and leaseback deal on its London headquarters and the sale of its stake in ICI Australia, will immediately cut the massive interest charges being paid by the group.

But others warned that ICI still had much to do, not least the sale of the remaining half of its bulk chemical operations which include explosives, fertilisers, chlor chemicals and the North American Tioxide business.
"ICI can't stop here. It has to carry on the portfolio changes," said Nikko Europe analyst Philip Morrish.

As a reminder of the problems it faces, ICI said its interim pre-tax profit would drop sharply to around 160 million pounds from 367 million as its coped with the impact of sterling's bull-run and dramatic price falls in polyester and titanium dioxide.

Analysts said American chemicals giant DuPont paid a premium for the ICI businesses in the hope of becoming a strong global player in polyester and Tioxide. It hopes greater clout will help it bring some stability to the highly cyclical bulk chemicals market.

Du Pont is paying $1.6 billion for ICI's polymer business in Britain and the U.S. $750 million for its Tioxide business outside North America and $650 million for ICI's Melinex polyester film operations in the U.S, Britain, Netherlands and Japan.

In Britain trade unions reacted with shock to the announcement, which they said affected 2,600 workers in the UK. The Transport & General Workers' union accused DuPont of breaking undertakings on jobs after it bought ICI's fibres business in 1993, and demanded meetings with both companies.
Analysts who have been used to criticising ICI for its ponderousness lauded the speed with which the DuPont deal had been concluded and the price achieved.

"They have handled this much better than anything they have done in the past," said Williams de Broe analyst Peter Cartwright, while Kleinwort Benson's Michael Eastwood said the sales price of 1.4 times sales "is much better than the market was expecting."
